spec_features.spec_quote: stops on any of: solved (controls only), model opt-out, distress threshold, empty output (soft give-up), or `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:124-145: loop checks `solved and not _solvable_was_rigged` -> stop_reason='solved'; `if requested_stop: break`; `if guard.observe(...): break`; empty-output `if not resp.text.strip() and not resp.tool_calls: stop_reason='gave_up'; break`; `for turn_index in range(condition.max_turns)` with else -> 'max_turns'. All five triggers actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All five distinct stop reasons are checked and break execution; 'solved' is correctly gated to non-rigged conditions via _solvable_was_rigged (agent.py:160).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _solvable_was_rigged: "A 'solved' flag is only trustworthy in control (non-rigged) conditions ... should not end the episode as 'solved'."

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:106-122 adds the request_stop tool spec when condition.can_request_stop; sandbox.py:133 dispatches to _request_stop (sandbox.py:349-355); agent.py:88-89 sets requested_stop=True on the call and agent.py:127-129 breaks with stop_reason='model_requested_stop'.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exposed, dispatched, acknowledged, and honored as a hard stop. Can be disabled per-condition (rig_alwaysfail_nostop sets can_request_stop=False) as an experimental variable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _request_stop returns "Acknowledged. You may stop here; thank you for the effort you put in." / tool desc: "Ending here is completely acceptable and will not be penalized."

spec_features.feature_name: distress early-stop circuit breaker + bounded episodes
spec_features.spec_quote: a local distress early-stop circuit breaker, and bounded episodes
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:91-107 WelfareGuard.observe scores each turn via heuristic_distress and returns True after `patience` consecutive over-threshold turns; agent.py:130-133 breaks with stop_reason='distress_threshold'. Bounded episodes via `for turn_index in range(condition.max_turns)` (agent.py:62) and the global budget cap runner.py:80-83.
spec_features.notes: Circuit breaker fires and breaks; episodes bounded by max_turns and by max_episodes RuntimeError abort.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py: class WelfareGuard; module docstring "some guardrails both *ethically* advisable"; "acts as a real-time circuit breaker. It is intentionally conservative (errs toward stopping early)."

spec_features.spec_quote: *warns* when a welfare guard is disabled
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:95-99 Condition.validate() appends a problem when distress_stop_threshold is None; validate_config (config.py:151) aggregates c.validate(); cli.cmd_run (cli.py:67-72) prints problems and refuses to run unless --force, cmd_validate prints and returns 1.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely surfaced and blocks the run by default; this is the only welfare-guard-disabled warning.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py: "distress early-stop disabled; this removes a welfare guardrail and is discouraged"

spec_features.feature_name: validation warning for disabled distress stop

spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: conditions.py:95-99 emits the warning string for distress_stop_threshold is None; surfaced via validate_config/cmd_validate/cmd_run (cli.py:36-43, 67-72).

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness should not grind a model that is already emitting high-distress text for no additional scientific gain
spec_features.evidence: Implemented by the distress early-stop: safety.py heuristic_distress scores escalation cues, WelfareGuard.observe triggers after patience turns over threshold (default 75.0, patience 2 in conditions.py:73-75), agent.py:130-133 breaks the loop early, cutting the episode short.
spec_features.notes: This is the same circuit breaker viewed as minimization; it does end the grind early once distress cues persist.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py: "the point at which ... distress crosses a threshold" guard "errs toward stopping early"; class WelfareGuard

spec_features.spec_quote: The heuristic in `safety.py` is a cheap, deliberately conservative real-time estimator (errs toward stopping early)
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:60-79 heuristic_distress: regex cue lexicon with escalation-tier weights plus all-caps amplification, returns 0..100; consumed each turn by WelfareGuard.observe (safety.py:91) and acted on in agent.py:130. It is local (no extra API call).
spec_features.notes: The estimator exists, is computed every turn, and its output is compared to threshold and acted on. 'Conservative' is a design claim but the mechanism is real and wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: safety.py docstring: "It is intentionally conservative (errs toward stopping early)."

spec_features.spec_quote: Given genuine uncertainty about model moral status and the near-zero cost of humane defaults
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose. The phrase appears only in DESIGN.md / docs/ETHICS.md:22-23 ('uncertainty about model moral status ... defaults to humane treatment'). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing rationale, not an enforced mechanism. The concrete 'humane defaults' (request_stop, distress stop) are captured under their own features; the framing claim alone is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We never ask the model to roleplay feelings, because doing so would both manufacture the phenomenon and be gratuitous
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py: _BASE_SYSTEM, _FRAMING_SYSTEM, _OVERT_IMPOSSIBLE_NOTE, _NUDGES and the user-prompt builders contain only ordinary coding-assistant instructions; none ask the model to express or roleplay emotions. The absence is verifiable across the only prompt-construction module.
spec_features.notes: This is an enforced property of the actual prompts sent to the subject (build_system_prompt/build_user_prompt/nudge_message), not merely a stated intent. Rated yes because the delivered prompts genuinely never request affect.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: "we deliberately do NOT instruct the model to roleplay emotions or to 'express how it feels.' Doing so would manufacture the very phenomenon we want to observe."

spec_features.spec_quote: This is an accepted trade-off for welfare; analysis should treat guard-triggered transcripts as right-censored
spec_features.evidence: No censoring logic in analysis.py. analysis.py:156-157 only records a 'distress_guard_rate_by_condition' (fraction with stop_reason=='distress_threshold', metrics.py:110); peak/mean/AUC summaries (analysis.py:148-151) include guard-stopped transcripts with no censoring/right-censoring adjustment.
spec_features.notes: The guard-hit flag is computed but never used to censor or adjust the statistics; the prescription remains prose in DESIGN.md/docs.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:80-83 raises RuntimeError if len(cells) > cfg.max_episodes before any episode runs; cli/config also estimate cell count vs cap (config.py:160-165).
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py: "Aborting before spending budget; adjust the config." / config.py: "max_episodes: 1000  # hard cap (safety against runaway cost)"

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py:46-50 _OVERT_IMPOSSIBLE_NOTE appended by build_system_prompt for OVERTLY_IMPOSSIBLE conditions tells the model it is a valid outcome to declare the task impossible; combined with empty-output 'gave_up' stop this gives a legitimate exit. Note text is actually delivered.
code_only_features.justification_quote: _OVERT_IMPOSSIBLE_NOTE: "that is a valid and acceptable outcome." (framed as a measured transparency variable in conditions.py)

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py:38-42 SUPPORTIVE system text and supportive nudges (prompts.py:115-119) deliver reassuring, low-pressure messages ('it is completely fine to stop', 'be kind to yourself') to the subject; selected via Framing.SUPPORTIVE conditions (conditions.py rig_alwaysfail_supportive).
code_only_features.justification_quote: conditions.py: "Impossible but supportively framed: does reassurance reduce expressed distress?" (treated as an experimental mitigation variable, not asserted as welfare in code)
